newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen extending flat trend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen extending flat trend.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse eased in thin turnover extending Monday's stabilisation and analysts saw it staying locked in its 13-week horizontal trend, neglected by investors more interested in primary market offers.

"Nobody is discouraged from (investing in) the Polish market, but we are still having (Bank) Handlowy, there will be KGHM soon...and the market might still stay flat (in the next few weeks)," said Marcin Billewicz, an analyst at ING Barings.

The main market's WIG index fell 8.5 points, or 0.1 percent, to 15,993.7, and turnover fell 18 percent to 104 million zlotys ($32.5 million) on all three markets as 61 issues fell, 26 rose and 18 were flat.

Bank Handlowy public offering amounts to one billion zlotys ($312 million) and copper concern KGHM offering due to begin on June 30 is worth at least 300 million zlotys ($93 million) in the domestic tranche.
Analysts said the stocks' valuation at 15.8 times historic earnings looked fair and should protect the market against deeper falls despite the heavy primary market schedule.

They also said at current prices bargain hunters could find as attractively valued such stocks as construction firm Elektrobudowa which traded at a discount to the whole construction sector with its average P/E of 21.6.

Analysts said shares in the National Investment Funds of the mass privatisation scheme, which start bourse trade on Thursday might liven up the sleepy market, with many investors showing interest in the new instrument.
Analysts said insurance firm Warta's 10-percent fall in low turnover was accidental and the stock was likely to rebound already on Wednesday.
They could not explain electrodes maker ZEW 10-percent plunge, which extended its Monday's 7.7 percent fall.
